prompt: The shop's site stops loading the help widget. What does the assistant's error rate show?

choices.text: Nothing unusual
choices.why: Right. Nobody asks, nothing fails. Only volume against last week sees it.

choices.text: A spike, because requests fail to arrive
choices.why: A request that never arrives is never counted as anything.

choices.text: A rise in refusals from the search
choices.why: Refusals need questions, and none arrive.

choices.text: A rise in timeouts against the provider
choices.why: No call is made, so none can time out.

prompt: Why can a refusal rate computed between midnight and six look alarming every night?

choices.text: Because the provider is slower at night
choices.why: Speed has nothing to do with refusals.

choices.text: Because it is a rate over a handful of requests
choices.why: Right. A few refusals among ten requests is a large rate and a small fact.

choices.text: Because night questions are harder to answer from the documents
choices.why: The traffic draws the same topics at every hour.

choices.text: Because the floor is higher at night
choices.why: The floor depends on the release, not the hour.

prompt: How many requests did the busiest day of the week have?
Why does the error count of lesson 4 miss most of the assistant's failures?

choices.text: Because errors.py has a bug in how it reads status
choices.why: It counted the failures it was asked to count.

choices.text: Because failures were not recorded on spans
choices.why: Outcomes are on every root span; they are just not errors.

choices.text: Because the replay hides failures
choices.why: The replay records everything the assistant does.

choices.text: They are answers
choices.why: Right: no exception is raised. A wrong refusal is a successful request to anything that counts errors.

prompt: Under release 2026.10.1, what percentage of order requests were refused?
No dangling citations appeared all week. Why keep the column?

choices.text: Because llama3.2:3b invents citations on most days
choices.why: It did not invent one all week; the zero is real.

choices.text: Because the column is needed by the cost report
choices.why: costs.py does not read it.

choices.text: Because an invented source number would show up nowhere else
choices.why: Right. A zero this week says nothing about the next model or prompt.

choices.text: To fill the table
choices.why: A column with no possible reading would be cut.

prompt: The order message scored 0.537 with the customer's details and 0.635 without. Why the difference?

choices.text: The redaction changed the meaning of the question
choices.why: The question was the same; the details were the difference.

choices.text: The name and address pull the embedding away from the documents
choices.why: Right. The documents contain none of them.

choices.text: Longer messages always score lower, whatever they contain
choices.why: It is what the extra words are, not how many.

choices.text: The order number matched a different document better
choices.why: No document contains order numbers of that shape.

prompt: Where does this lesson point the fix for the order questions?

choices.text: Lower the floor back to 0.4
choices.why: That helps both features, but the order questions refused more even at 0.4.

choices.text: Remove the order feature until it can be rebuilt from scratch
choices.why: The cause is narrow and has a narrow fix.

choices.text: Give the search the question, not the whole message
choices.why: Right. Strip the details or restate the question before retrieving.

choices.text: Use a bigger model
choices.why: The model never saw these questions: the search refused them first.

prompt: What made going from the refusal rate to the cause possible?

choices.text: The thumbs down on the order questions
choices.why: A thumb says something was wrong, not what.

choices.text: The cost report broken down by feature for the week
choices.why: Cost does not say why a search kept nothing.

choices.text: The volume by hour
choices.why: The hour has nothing to do with this cause.

choices.text: The traces carried the search's top score
choices.why: Right. A trace explains only what its attributes recorded.

prompt: How is a thumb joined to the reply it judges?

choices.text: By its trace id
choices.why: Right: the one the screen received with the reply. The join is exact.

choices.text: By the user and the closest reply in time
choices.why: Two questions a minute apart would be confused.

choices.text: By the session
choices.why: A session holds several replies.

choices.text: By position in the file
choices.why: Feedback is written in the order it happens, not the order of replies.

prompt: Thumbs down were 16% of ratings under one release and 15% under the next. Why compare releases of the same screen and not two products?

choices.text: Because other products do not show thumbs
choices.why: Many do; that is not the reason.

choices.text: Because thumbs are only collected for one release
choices.why: They were collected in both.

choices.text: Because 15% is too low to be real
choices.why: Nothing makes 15% implausible.

choices.text: Who rates depends on the design, so the crowd differs
choices.why: Right. A thumbs-down rate measures the raters, and the raters are chosen by the design.

prompt: A dashboard shows a day's thumbs-down rate from about twenty ratings. What should a reader expect of it?

choices.text: It will jump about from day to day on noise alone
choices.why: Right. Lesson 9 puts a margin of error on a rate like this.

choices.text: It will be steadier than the rephrasing rate
choices.why: The rephrasing rate is counted over every request and moves on far less noise.

choices.text: It will be zero, because so few people rate
choices.why: Twenty ratings give a rate, just an unsteady one.

choices.text: It will equal the refusal rate, since every refusal gets a thumbs down
choices.why: Only some customers rate, and right refusals get thumbs up.

prompt: Under release 2026.09.4, how many thumbs down were there?
Why do rephrasing and asking for a person move on less noise than thumbs?

choices.text: They are recorded by the provider
choices.why: The provider knows nothing about sessions.

choices.text: They happen more often than a thumbs down on any given day of the week
choices.why: Frequency is not why; the denominator is.

choices.text: Everyone's next move is counted, not only the raters'
choices.why: Right. Everybody does something next; only some click.

choices.text: They are averaged over the week
choices.why: So are the thumbs in signals.py.

prompt: In real traffic, how does the lesson tell a rephrasing from a follow-up question?

choices.text: By the time between them alone
choices.why: A follow-up comes just as quickly.

choices.text: By whether the second embedding is close to the first
choices.why: Right. Same session, soon after, and close in meaning.

choices.text: By asking the customer which it was
choices.why: That would be a survey nobody answers.

choices.text: By the length of the second question
choices.why: Length says nothing about whether it repeats the first.

prompt: What does a handover to a person need, to count as a verdict on a reply?

choices.text: The last reply's trace id
choices.why: Right. Without it, it is a staffing number.

choices.text: The customer's name, to follow up later
choices.why: The name joins to nothing in the traces, and lesson 2 keeps it out.

choices.text: A thumbs down first
choices.why: Most customers never rate.

choices.text: A record in the provider's log
choices.why: The provider never sees the handover.

prompt: Under the new release, rephrasings nearly ___ per hundred requests, from 6.7 to 12.8.
Why read cost and satisfaction in one view rather than in two reports?

choices.text: To save a query
choices.why: The cost of a query is not the point.

choices.text: Because cost causes dissatisfaction
choices.why: Both had a common cause; neither caused the other.

choices.text: One event caused both
choices.why: Right. Two reports would show it as two pieces of news; the release made the assistant cheaper by making it worse.

choices.text: Because satisfaction cannot be measured alone
choices.why: This lesson measured it alone first.

prompt: Which failure is invisible to every number in lessons 1 to 5?

choices.text: A refusal to a question the documents answer
choices.why: The refusal rate counts those, and customers rephrase after them.

choices.text: A confident wrong answer the customer believes
choices.why: Right. No thumb, no rephrasing, no handover. Lessons 8 to 13 build what sees it.

choices.text: A provider outage
choices.why: Lesson 4's error rates see it.

choices.text: A rise in cost per request
choices.why: Lesson 3's bill sees it.

prompt: On Thursday 1 October, the day of the release, what percentage of help and order requests were refused?
Match each signal to what it is evidence of.

pairs.left: a drop in volume against last week

pairs.right: customers told the documents have nothing
the assistant failed to help, at a price

items: split it by feature and release
pick a few traces behind it

prompt: Which signals in this lesson were counted over every request, not only over those who chose to give them? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: The refusal rate
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Rephrasing
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Thumbs down
choices.why: Only those who rated.

choices.text: Asking for a person
choices.why: Right.
